name: Manufacturing and Mechatronics Technician
description: Manufacturing technicians keep automated production running — controls, robotics, instrumentation and the mechanical systems underneath — by following a fault across electrical, mechanical and software boundaries. ⚠ Florida's entry certificate is 300 hours, the shortest on this site, and the training travels much further than the job title suggests.
credentialNote: ⚠ No licence governs this work, and the certifications are the currency instead. The usual first one is the MSSC Certified Production Technician, which Florida's 300-hour Certified Production Technology certificate is built against — four assessments covering safety, quality practices and measurement, manufacturing processes and production, and maintenance awareness. ⚠⚠ After that the certifications that matter are the ones the plants near you run: the control-platform certificates (Allen-Bradley, Siemens) and, in regulated industries, the quality-system training that goes with medical devices or aerospace. Ask a programme which certifications its graduates hold and which local employers hire them — in this field that answer is the qualification.
bodyHtml:
What the work actually is

O*NET: operate, test, maintain or adjust unmanned, automated, servomechanical or electromechanical equipment. The tasks span three trades at once — test electromechanical assemblies using instruments such as oscilloscopes and voltmeters; install or program computer hardware and microprocessor-based system software; read blueprints and technical documents to determine assembly methods; modify and repair electrical, electronic or mechanical components; inspect parts for surface defects and verify dimensions against specifications.

⚠ That combination is the whole point of the job. A plant has electricians, mechanics and programmers; the technician who can follow a fault across all three — sensor to controller to actuator — is the one who gets a line running again, and is paid accordingly.

Projected need

O*NET, on federal projections for electro-mechanical and mechatronics technicians: 15,000 employed (2024), growth “slower than average (1% to 2%)”, 1,300 openings a year, median wages $73,900 (2025). Education: 32% a post-secondary certificate, 30% an associate degree, 11% a bachelor’s.

⚠ Read that occupation code carefully — it is narrow, and the training is not. 15,000 people nationally is a small occupation, and if you judge this path by that number alone you will misjudge it. The same certificates feed industrial machinery mechanics, electrical and electronics repairers, quality inspectors, process operators and production supervisors — occupations with hundreds of thousands of jobs between them. The narrow title pays well; the training travels much further than the title does.

⚠⚠ The fastest credential on this site, and what it is for

Certified Production Technology is 300 hours — a single completion point, and by some distance the shortest programme here. It exists to get someone hireable in a plant quickly, and it is built against the MSSC Certified Production Technician assessments: safety, quality practices and measurement, manufacturing processes and production, and maintenance awareness.

⚠ Treat it as a door rather than a destination. It gets you inside a manufacturer, where the ladder — and frequently the tuition assistance — is. The 1,200-hour industrial machinery and controls route is where the technician wage actually sits.

⚠⚠⚠ The 2025 framework exists; the courses do not yet

Florida published Industrial Machinery and Controls Technician in 2025 — 1,200 hours, four completion points from assistant through technician II. ⚠ Its four course numbers are carried by NO Florida institution in the statewide numbering system. The framework is ahead of the colleges; what they are still teaching is the predecessor set:

  • Production technology — production worker, assembler, process assistant and automation and production technology, four institutions each, 150 hours apiece.
  • Industrial machinery maintenance — assistant, mechanic, technician and specialist, four to five institutions, 150–450 hours.
  • Mechatronics and electronics technician courses at three to eight institutions.

⚠ So do not go looking for the 2025 course numbers. Ask a programme what it delivers, how many hours, and which certifications it prepares you for — and expect the answer to name the older courses for a while yet. This site lists both, and says which is which.

Necessary skills

  • Electrical diagnosis with instruments — meters, oscilloscopes, and the discipline to test rather than guess.
  • Controls and PLC logic. ⚠ The skill that separates this trade from general maintenance: reading ladder logic, tracing an I/O fault, and knowing what the program is asking the machine to do.
  • Mechanical fundamentals — bearings, drives, alignment, hydraulics and pneumatics. Half of an automation fault is mechanical.
  • Measurement and quality — calipers, micrometers, tolerance and the reason a part is rejected.
  • Working under a line stoppage. ⚠ Methodical diagnosis while a plant loses money by the minute is the real test, and it is a temperament as much as a skill.

Advice

  • Start with the 300-hour certificate if you need income sooner, then let an employer help with the rest. Manufacturers with hard-to-fill technician roles frequently pay for further training, and being inside is the qualification for that.
  • ⚠ Ask specifically about PLCs and robotics. Programmes differ enormously here — some teach a current Allen-Bradley or Siemens platform on real hardware, others cover controls in principle. It is the difference in employability.
  • Chase the certifications employers name — MSSC CPT to start, and whatever platform certification the plants near you run.
  • Florida's manufacturing is specific: aerospace and space-launch suppliers, medical devices, food and beverage, boat building, and building products. ⚠ The plants are regional, so ask a programme which local employers hire its graduates — the good ones answer with names.
  • ⚠ Read the electrician path beside this one. The first year overlaps heavily, the licensing story is completely different, and people regularly discover in year two that they wanted the other one.

programs.note: The programme itself — 28 Florida public institutions across the electromechanical and instrumentation codes, from a 300-hour entry certificate to the 1,200-hour technician sequence.

⚠ The fork worth understanding early: much of the first year is shared, but an electrician wires buildings under a licensing regime while a manufacturing technician keeps machines running inside one. People discover in year two that they wanted the other.
⚠ The degree route above the certificates — automation engineering, maintenance planning and supervision — and the usual way a technician's pay stops being hourly.
